newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cap. Intelligence upgrades Iktisat Bankasi rating.
newsitem.headline: Cap. Intelligence upgrades Iktisat Bankasi rating.

text.p: Cyprus-based Capital Intelligence on Tuesday said it had upgraded the long-term rating of Iktisat Bankasi of Turkey to BB from BB-.
The short-term rating was maintained at A-3, the specialist bank rating agency announced.
"Aided by the enhanced structure of its balance sheet, Iktisat is now in a better position to capitalise on market opportunities," said Capital Intelligence in a news release.

"The bank holds a strong position in trade in Turkey. Business activity in this area will remain robust, due to the trading nature of the Turkish economy in addition to growing opportunities stemming from Turkey's customs union with the European Union.
However, competition will remain intense as banks compete for market share," Capital Intelligence said.
Capital Intelligence said an improvement in loan asset quality of the bank was recorded in 1996, despite non-performing loans remaining at 9 percent of total loans.
The majority, 74 percent, of non-performing loans is historical, relating to exposure of US $32 million to two banks in Iraq. However, the bank has now fully provided for the total exposure.

A reversal of the funding mix back to bank borrowings occurred in 1996, with deposits rising by only 59 percent in lira terms. However, at 43 percent of total liabilities and capital, Iktisat still has a good deposit base for a wholesale institution. Nevertheless, the increased reliance on borrowings may cause difficulties if the perceived risk of the market deteriorates quickly, the agency said.

Capital Intelligence said profitability accelerated in 1996. The main factor behind the increase was the substantial rise in net income, which moved up by over 200 percent in US $ terms to US$ 75 million.
Reflecting higher yields on securities, in combination with a better performing loan portfolio, the bank's interest differential rose to 20 percent from 13 percent in 1996.
Net profit for the year amounted to $50 million, Capital Intelligence said.

Iktisat, a medium sized bank, was established in 1927 and is owned by the Aksoy Group which has interests in the financial services and media sectors. Assets at year-end 1996 stood at US $1,034 million.

By acquiring and establishing subsidiaries, Iktisat has built an international group of financial services companies, including Banque Internationale de Commerce in Paris and the Park Avenue Bank in New York, as well as leasing, factoring and insurance companies, said Capital Intelligence.
